guitar.evidence: Wilson Pickett was a soul vocalist, not a guitarist; backing was via session musicians (Muscle Shoals/Stax players) that varied by recording.
guitar.notes: Correctly left unknown — not a guitar-led act.

tone.target: tight clean-soul twang with rhythmic wah and light grit
tone.profile: tight clean-soul twang with rhythmic wah and light grit
tone.summary: A classic soul/R&B setup utilizing light compression and a British combo amp model (UK 50) paired with the V-Wah for rhythmic, twangy leads and rhythm work.

rig.name: Wilson Pickett - In The Midnight Hour - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and maintain tight rhythm.
Provide a slight lift and snappy attack for the rhythm guitar.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of OD/Comp to maintain maximum clarity while adding punch.

blocks.purpose: The signature rhythmic wah swells required for the soul genre.
Provide light grit and edge without heavy distortion.
blocks.gap: Using the 'None' setting on a dedicated drive block to simulate minimal breakup/overdrive, keeping gain low as requested.

blocks.purpose: Simulate a small-to-mid combo amp with punchy, articulate clean tones.
Provide a classic British cabinet sound that complements the UK 50 amp model.
Enhance the percussive mid-focus and tighten the overall tone.
Optional subtle modulation for depth (kept off by default to avoid lush sound).
blocks.gap: Chorus was listed in 'avoid', but a very subtle setting can add dimension without sounding too lush.

blocks.purpose: Used sparingly for rhythmic accents only.
blocks.gap: Delay is generally avoided in pure soul/R&B, but included as a subtle option.

blocks.purpose: Provide a minimal sense of space without sounding lush or overly wet.
blocks.gap: The requirement was to avoid 'lush reverb', so the mix and decay time are kept very low.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism for a tighter, more percussive soul sound.

proposals.reason: A smaller/different cab will tighten the low end and focus on mid-range punch.
